 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Narayanswamy S/o Late Ramayya in a Road Traffic accident.
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3855/2023 2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 12.06.2023 at about 11.15 p.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Sri. Narayanswamy was riding his scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-50-V-4631 and reached near Puttenahalli Bus Depo, Doddaballapura main road, Yelahanka,
Bengaluru, at that time, one Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-88-6588 was parked in the middle of road, without any indicator and Narayanswamy has lost his control on his Scooter and dashed against the lorry and fell down and sustained grievous head injury and died on the spot.
Thereafter, the Post Mortem was conducted at Government Hospital, Yelahanka and dead body was handed over to the Petitioners.
The Petitioners had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was doing business and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The Petitioners were entirely SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3855/2023 depending upon the income of the deceased.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-88-6588.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.2 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection Statement to the main petition.

The Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the negligent parking and rash and negligent Gayathri vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191659633/
2 driving of the offending lorry by its driver and also the death of the Narayanswamy due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Further it contended that the said accident has taken place due to the negligence of the deceased rider and as on the date of accident the rider did not possess the valid DL.
SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3855/2023
Further, it contended that the deceased did not wear helmet at the time of accident.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

On these grounds,
the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Narayanswamy S/o Late Ramayya was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 12.06.2023 at about 11.15 p.m., near Puttenahalli Bus Depo, Doddaballapura main road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-88-6588?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Narayanswamy?

3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
 SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3855/2023  4) What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents at Ex.P.1 to 12 and closed her side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any evidence.
But, it got marked one document at Ex.R1 with the consent of Petitioners.

6. Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :

REASONS 7. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that the SCCH 15 7 MVC No.3855/2023 husband of the Gayathri vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191659633/
3

Petitioner No.1 by name Narayanswamy was died in the road traffic accident that occurred due to the negligent parking of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-88-6588.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident occurred by the negligent parking of the driver of the offending lorry.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the petition.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P12.

Ex.P-1 and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by Karthik N S/o Narayan Swamy R, the Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-88-6588 for the offences SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3855/2023 punishable under Sections 283 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot mahazar with Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 & 5 are the Accident Inspection Report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

Ex.P-6 is the true copy of the Charge-Sheet which shows that the I.O of the Yelahanka Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending lorry for the offences punishable under Sections 283 and 304(A) of IPC.

Ex.P7 is the copy of PM report which shows the cause of death is due to cardio respiratory arrest which is due to crush injury of right lung with haveothorax and splenic ruptured resulted in haveothonlum which occurred due to road traffic accident.
Ex.P8 is the Inquest Mahazar of the deceased.
Ex.P9 to 11 are the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners and deceased.
Ex.P12 is the DL of the deceased.
11. P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1.

But,
nothing could SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3855/2023 be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any evidence.
Hence, it failed to substantiate its Objection statement contentions.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioners and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that PW.1 has proved the negligent parking of the offending lorry without putting indicators and without taking precautions and thereby the accident has occurred and in the said accident, her husband was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."
12. Issue No.2

and 3 : Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.
13.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
Petitioner No.2 & 3 are son and daughter of the deceased Narayanswamy.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3855/2023 PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.1 and 2 and deceased at Ex.P.9 to 11.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to rely on the Judgments of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka which are as under:

sentences.text: 14. In the above Judgments of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to held that the major children are not dependent and they entitled only Consortium as per the Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi and Magma General Insurance Company Limited.
In the instant case also, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the SCCH 15 11 MVC No.3855/2023 major son and major daughter of the deceased.
No evidence has been adduced to show that the petitioner No.2 and 3 are financially dependents on the deceased.
Hence, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are not dependents and petitioner No.1 is only dependent of the deceased.
15. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 65 years and deceased was doing a business and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, PW.1 has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,000/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
16. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Narayanswamy was 65 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.12 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Narayanswamy which shows his date of birth was 16.08.1958.
The alleged accident has been occurred on 12.06.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3855/2023 Narayanswamy was 64 years, 09 months and 26 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Narayanswamy to be taken at 65 years for the purpose of assessment.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind him his wife and children.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the son and daughter.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-,
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3855/2023 loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount Gayathri vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191659633/
5 should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

sentences.text: The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

19. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the wife and children of the deceased Narayanswamy, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
20.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3855/2023 love and care and support.
Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the son and daughter and they lost their father's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
21. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
22.
It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was taken at Rs.16,000/- pm.

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3855/2023 No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: "There should be no addition after 60 years.".

The income of the deceased was taken at Rs.16,000/- p.m..
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 7.

sentences.text: As per the detailed discussion made above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 is the only dependent of deceased Narayanswamy.
Hence, 1/2 of the income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenses.

23. After deducting 1/2 towards his personal expenses in Rs.16,000/- it comes to Rs.8,000/-
(Rs.16,000/- - 8,000/-) and multiplier applied is 7 which comes to Rs.6,72,000/- (Rs.8,000 x 12 x 7).
Thus, the Petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,72,000/- towards loss of dependency.

TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of Consortium Rs. 1,45,200/-
(48,400X3)
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,150/-
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/-
of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs. 6,72,000/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are awarded compensation of Rs.9,08,500/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

25. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the negligent SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3855/2023 parking on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-88-6588.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.

The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2,
has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner No.1 to 3.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,08,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 SCCH 15 18 MVC No.3855/2023 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,08,500/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
